title: Hearty Springy Algerian Lentil Tagine
description: A traditional Algerian dish featuring lentils, molasses, and nuka-pickle, this tagine is a bitter, springy, and nostalgic meal, satvik-friendly and perfect for a weeknight dinner.
instructions: In a large pot, heat 2 tablespoons of oil over medium heat.
Add the chopped onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add the minced garlic and grated ginger and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in the cumin, paprika, salt, and black pepper and cook for 1 minute.
Add the rinsed lentils, molasses, and chopped nuka-pickle, and stir to combine.
Add 2 cups of water and bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat to low and simmer, covered, for 30 minutes.
Serve hot, garnished with chopped fresh parsley or cilantro.
Note: this recipe is for refrigerator pickling/preserving only — store in the refrigerator and consume within 1 week. Do not water-bath can without an acid (vinegar or lemon juice).
